59: // ClientFilterBuilder is an optional interface that a Builder can implement to
60: // indicate its capability to build client-side filters.
61: type ClientFilterBuilder interface {
62: 	// BuildClientFilter constructs a ClientFilter. The ClientFilter's Close
63: 	// method is to be invoked when the filter is no longer needed.
64: 	BuildClientFilter() (filter ClientFilter)
65: }
66: 
67: // ClientFilter represents the actual filter implementation on the client side.
68: // Implementations are free to maintain internal state when required, and share
69: // it across interceptors. Filter instances are retained by the resolver as long
70: // as they are present in the LDS configuration.
71: type ClientFilter interface {
72: 	// BuildClientInterceptor uses the given FilterConfigs to produce an HTTP
73: 	// filter interceptor for clients. config will always be non-nil, but
74: 	// override may be nil if no override config exists for the filter.
75: 	//
76: 	// It is valid for this method to return a nil Interceptor and a nil error.
77: 	// In this case, the RPC will not be intercepted by this filter.
78: 	//
79: 	// The returned cleanup function is to be invoked when the interceptor is no
80: 	// longer needed.
81: 	BuildClientInterceptor(config, override FilterConfig) (interceptor iresolver.ClientInterceptor, cleanup func(), err error)
82: 
83: 	// Close releases any resources held by the filter. It is to be invoked
84: 	// when the filter is no longer needed.
85: }

88: // ServerFilterBuilder is an optional interface that a Builder can implement to
89: // indicate its capability to build server-side filters.
90: type ServerFilterBuilder interface {

92: 	// is to be invoked when the filter is no longer needed.

96: // ServerFilter represents the actual filter implementation on the server side.
97: // Implementations are free to maintain internal state when required, and share
98: // it across interceptors. Filter instances are retained by the server as long
99: // as they are present in any of the filter chains in the LDS configuration.
100: type ServerFilter interface {
101: 	// BuildServerInterceptor uses the given FilterConfigs to produce
102: 	// an HTTP filter interceptor for servers. config will always be non-nil,
103: 	// but override may be nil if no override config exists for the filter.
104: 	//
105: 	// It is valid for this method to return a nil Interceptor and a nil error.
106: 	// In this case, the RPC will not be intercepted by this filter.
107: 	//
108: 	// The returned cleanup function is to be invoked when the interceptor is no
109: 	// longer needed.
110: 	BuildServerInterceptor(config, override FilterConfig) (interceptor iresolver.ServerInterceptor, cleanup func(), err error)
111: }
